[Highlight start] **No, throwing up will not cure a hangover** [Highlight end] , and forcing yourself to vomit is generally not recommended. Alcohol is absorbed into your bloodstream quickly, so vomiting hours later—or once hangover symptoms set in—does not remove alcohol already circulating in your body or clear the toxic byproducts causing your symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXRmgBwPrbkn6qCSjWpwZbecHV_c-RPa4byyHriQL2QEDOH6BNpeWvqqu6dkC6-fW8Xt7e_2GyNFP2LOyXiEVo4a-5OUeUa0dwymmSw4KNaMuy9Trhi7ZztL1SL9aIwlZxGOrl1uOsRdDFKKXqKDLvCYwuFA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF19utG0AATl4KBhvEmINOY8Y6n6xeB4Ovfz4GI7Y_uvHMcc5Qjb263hh4By5pyCRDLQe37ndGwczYT_E1VZv4C5SY28bY6kHE5vIewQwFUa0vKOmYLjzALdDWt4jlxE2-0WtEJepu06X50vaga79Jax3uFAWHfIYpOzHQyWo3Kg)

### Why Throwing Up Usually Doesn't Help

- **Worsens dehydration:** Hangovers involve fluid and electrolyte loss, and vomiting drains even more fluids.
- **Irritates your digestive tract:** Stomach acid and alcohol coming back up can inflame your esophagus, irritate your stomach lining, and harm tooth enamel.
- **Carries safety risks:** Forcing yourself to throw up while intoxicated increases risks like choking or inhaling vomit into your lungs.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXRq0q6ypokb9BE_uHKBYjYS_h2fTCDCfylgzeO5L7EdxiOop2oK6aDDlq2kXzUEgDvKFrLSY8DsUxN-VuC93ApnSSt0qmGp1mPHwG0n4p1HtyBsMVajM0wWJz5-0acH_lLfbNyXyyUx7h)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF19utG0AATl4KBhvEmINOY8Y6n6xeB4Ovfz4GI7Y_uvHMcc5Qjb263hh4By5pyCRDLQe37ndGwczYT_E1VZv4C5SY28bY6kHE5vIewQwFUa0vKOmYLjzALdDWt4jlxE2-0WtEJepu06X50vaga79Jax3uFAWHfIYpOzHQyWo3Kg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF11iC1wNDzoK-tqI_2QEGznK6JN5iMNRV2_xoF90YEyApnT6Jqdfx5xSvxPps9t7xR8IFcQJ3cBIwQWoBVfKuhCVosfcHLY2hiWIQzPi6tqqloVQgtgTD9ViZjNICqYB-ulJ48ZC4ws6EtthChO2U2z0dTr8SmPG8bqwtLVfsUKfgMmnM6YVQ7DarZXilxxR-MMCZ1TM)

### When It Might Feel Different

- **Right after drinking:** Vomiting very soon after drinking may remove unabsorbed alcohol still sitting in the stomach, though once alcohol is absorbed, throwing up won't undo its effects.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF19utG0AATl4KBhvEmINOY8Y6n6xeB4Ovfz4GI7Y_uvHMcc5Qjb263hh4By5pyCRDLQe37ndGwczYT_E1VZv4C5SY28bY6kHE5vIewQwFUa0vKOmYLjzALdDWt4jlxE2-0WtEJepu06X50vaga79Jax3uFAWHfIYpOzHQyWo3Kg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXRq0q6ypokb9BE_uHKBYjYS_h2fTCDCfylgzeO5L7EdxiOop2oK6aDDlq2kXzUEgDvKFrLSY8DsUxN-VuC93ApnSSt0qmGp1mPHwG0n4p1HtyBsMVajM0wWJz5-0acH_lLfbNyXyyUx7h)
- **Brief nausea relief:** Throwing up can temporarily ease stomach upset or nausea, but it does not fix dehydration, inflammation, or poor sleep. Most users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF13bvw3iECAccmVtr6XQuqVmFq94hlYM7p2z4aUVpqi6qrQsx8s1Tz-7EFSCbqn09RPihXGih21kXnhS6O6BU__N3dDGnonB3LmbcbNVnc59xs2qaCLKIlSOs8wmFLMqdblo_JjgTm-5leu4rLiJy8YAk8yo2i28U8t9u6oyPtdUSLxYqD6HFPXZGhf7aKAYvR67oEpsVJMwPzA) share a consensus that vomiting after heavy drinking can temporarily relieve nausea, even though it isn't a real hangover cure.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXgvE24UiZbzmumAZuKkL6DGK6zJs0Nsg3pp6h-uIPnXxrnG_VQ24BDiUFQeALBUfpJ9jvPQkowOJDbtwW7c958lLPjC-CwYdlZiikdmrZB57-bEzwl_ZD-mWc9mWiYCXqzAd-yIZf8nYFcGouFYb8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXRq0q6ypokb9BE_uHKBYjYS_h2fTCDCfylgzeO5L7EdxiOop2oK6aDDlq2kXzUEgDvKFrLSY8DsUxN-VuC93ApnSSt0qmGp1mPHwG0n4p1HtyBsMVajM0wWJz5-0acH_lLfbNyXyyUx7h)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF13bvw3iECAccmVtr6XQuqVmFq94hlYM7p2z4aUVpqi6qrQsx8s1Tz-7EFSCbqn09RPihXGih21kXnhS6O6BU__N3dDGnonB3LmbcbNVnc59xs2qaCLKIlSOs8wmFLMqdblo_JjgTm-5leu4rLiJy8YAk8yo2i28U8t9u6oyPtdUSLxYqD6HFPXZGhf7aKAYvR67oEpsVJMwPzA)

### What Actually Helps a Hangover
According to [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXRmgBwPrbkn6qCSjWpwZbecHV_c-RPa4byyHriQL2QEDOH6BNpeWvqqu6dkC6-fW8Xt7e_2GyNFP2LOyXiEVo4a-5OUeUa0dwymmSw4KNaMuy9Trhi7ZztL1SL9aIwlZxGOrl1uOsRdDFKKXqKDLvCYwuFA) , time is the only true cure while your body clears byproducts, rehydrates, and recovers. You can support your body by:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESswEBxCJF1_8xB4cs91zZh6MkfNCUhqXSk4GYqCRkC7xqz6byjP5PCkgoNegBsXNYjT88EstgxbU7tvYs-6U8UA2NEx1LmNJFedidwCOCzNJ9aPJMS9ZuXxc0_68HS7WLGe9of1Z7n3CTsyjKYjdhrZrWwXWVS7T5Xl4gBP6Taq8bDxHY6AmEDDCXPDzLd3AtR_8cw3fv_3f4HyAj6nlVwR5SscFe71OE5n3i6AeDJE4WUgdeqQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXRmgBwPrbkn6qCSjWpwZbecHV_c-RPa4byyHriQL2QEDOH6BNpeWvqqu6dkC6-fW8Xt7e_2GyNFP2LOyXiEVo4a-5OUeUa0dwymmSw4KNaMuy9Trhi7ZztL1SL9aIwlZxGOrl1uOsRdDFKKXqKDLvCYwuFA)

- Sipping water or electrolyte drinks slowly
- Eating bland carbohydrates like toast or crackers if your stomach settles
- Getting rest and letting time pass[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXIPvt6BWhbUd7eLOdXhGjbzxsfeMq0gpUNX3MkeSkVXfHJ7sa24dXtuKJ3dRQOdB7dRvTg51DcNFRd6bDc-7VRuowU0-HfITZmzCQA-l_cL5ZtWNgF2FrPI_6eOXus-Z7UtsGoUt0aK-G6BD-lvKZn_Tx)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXRmgBwPrbkn6qCSjWpwZbecHV_c-RPa4byyHriQL2QEDOH6BNpeWvqqu6dkC6-fW8Xt7e_2GyNFP2LOyXiEVo4a-5OUeUa0dwymmSw4KNaMuy9Trhi7ZztL1SL9aIwlZxGOrl1uOsRdDFKKXqKDLvCYwuFA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESswEBxCJF1_8xB4cs91zZh6MkfNCUhqXSk4GYqCRkC7xqz6byjP5PCkgoNegBsXNYjT88EstgxbU7tvYs-6U8UA2NEx1LmNJFedidwCOCzNJ9aPJMS9ZuXxc0_68HS7WLGe9of1Z7n3CTsyjKYjdhrZrWwXWVS7T5Xl4gBP6Taq8bDxHY6AmEDDCXPDzLd3AtR_8cw3fv_3f4HyAj6nlVwR5SscFe71OE5n3i6AeDJE4WUgdeqQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXDlKJ-eTo01P4LZqofxBjijZKg1riJ4wV1YG4NNCnjwGX6XxDXhdAo4cPG-rhNmrJHSuTl7Ft7mN0jZRUjJK34w2HbtvgLjO2t5qx7q0OUuwjfHosjTv4C8itSN-xP0y7FGAA9btXNenO1ycM4TAdVtZISu8XSP8f)
